title: Allcargo Terminals Ltd - 543954 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Allcargo Terminals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR208 crores and EBITDA 31% to INR44 crores; FY26 PAT up 46% to INR44 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes reached 179,631 TEUs (up 7% YoY, down 7% QoQ), with revenue of INR208 crores (up 12% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income of INR44 crores (up 31% YoY). EBITDA margin widened to 21.2% from 18% a year earlier, and Q4 net profit was INR9 crores versus a loss in Q4 FY25. For FY26, volumes were 723,035 TEUs (up 6%), revenue INR821 crores (up 8%), EBITDA INR162 crores (up 26%) and PAT INR44 crores (up 46%). Management reiterated a 1 million laden TEU target for FY28, a 2030 aspiration of 12.5-13 lakh laden TEU capacity, and an EBITDA per TEU target of about INR2,200-2,400.

segments.name: CFS and ICD (consolidated operations)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 EBITDA per TEU stated above INR2,000 and about INR2,400 per management's quarterly comments; FY26 EBITDA per TEU around INR2,200 per analyst read-through. Ground rent is near 20% of CFS revenue and declining as a share.

segments.name: JNPT Speedy Multimodes
segments.commentary: Facility contract extended 10 years; upgrade of yard and warehouses planned, with completion targeted around Q3 FY27, expected to lift throughput above pre-renewal levels. Facility size unchanged.

segments.name: Farrukhnagar PFT-ICD (rail-linked)
segments.commentary: Construction started January 2026 via group companies; PFT completion targeted April 2027, ICD about two quarters later. Expected to add about 1.2 lakh TEU capacity in phases and to be 20-25% of business once fully live.

guidance_outlook: 1 million laden TEU target reiterated for FY28, with management saying the company is on course.
2030 aspiration: capacity of about 12.5-13 lakh laden TEU, around 80% utilisation to reach 1 million TEU, and EBITDA per TEU rising from about INR2,300-2,400 to about INR2,800.
EBITDA per TEU steady-state target of INR2,200-2,400; management expects to maintain current levels.
Total capex of about INR400 crores for expansion projects: Farrukhnagar about INR200-226 crores, JNPT Speedy about INR20 crores, and the balance across Mundra and Chennai.
Lease outgo expected at INR95-100 crores per year on existing contracts, with no new lease contracts pending.
Market growth expected at 5-6% annually for containerised EXIM volumes.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 8.3 lakh TEU including Dadri ICD (JV with CONCOR), built up to about 1 million laden TEU during last year per management.
Farrukhnagar PFT-ICD: construction started January 2026; PFT completion targeted April 2027; ICD about two quarters later; about 1.2 lakh TEU added in phases.
JNPT Speedy Multimodes upgrade (around INR20 crores) targeted around Q3 FY27 to lift utilisation.
Chennai and Mundra expansions planned under the 3-year plan; Chennai details to be shared in future calls.
Estimated CFS market share about 10-12% (management caveat: no published figures).
demand_pricing: India GDP growth cited at 6-6.5%; major ports handled a record 915.2 million MT in FY26 (+7% YoY).
JNPA throughput grew about 7-7.5% last year per management; some recent terminal congestion and transport fleet shortage described as seasonal.
Ground rent realisation strengthened last year on commodity price changes and freight fluctuations, not disruptions; ground rent is near 20% of CFS revenue.
Quarterly EBITDA per TEU variation attributed to commodity mix, 20ft/40ft ratio, over-dimension cargo and auction spikes; management guides to steady state.
Management sees a competitive market and does not expect realisation gains from volume alone beyond the current EBITDA per TEU range.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Farrukhnagar ramp-up slower (about 70% utilisation only after FY30), and is any competing ICD coming up nearby?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the volume estimates conservative, based on current market study, with a review closer to launch; it knows of no competing new ICD in that location.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores total; Farrukhnagar about INR200-226 crores, JNPT Speedy about INR20 crores, rest for Mundra and Chennai. Existing investments of about INR45 crores and annual operating cash flow of INR80-90 crores; around INR300 crores to come from equity and cash flows, with bank or external debt capped near INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lease liability outgo and is the peak reached?
qa_highlights.answer: All lease extensions (CWC Mundra, JNPT, ATL-JNPT) are done; annual lease outgo expected at INR95-100 crores. Lease liability (about INR700 crores ROU liability shown as borrowings) should decline over time; company says it has no external debt.

qa_highlights.question: What drives EBITDA margin and EBITDA per TEU sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins run about 19-20% through the year; Q4 jump was partly from lower other expenses that may reverse. Steady-state EBITDA per TEU of INR2,200-2,400, with Farrukhnagar rail business expected to lift realisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation policy and further fundraise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is conserving capital; dividends and buybacks to be considered at an appropriate time. INR120 crores raised via rights issue and private placement, only first tranche called; about INR80 crores still to be called in the current year. No further equity planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: Are there opportunities from first-mile/last-mile, and ground rent upside from trade disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Transport and value-added services are offered via sister Allcargo group companies rather than booked in ATL revenue plans. Ground rent gains came from commodity and freight fluctuations, not disruption; it is now a declining share of revenue.

risks_watch: Farrukhnagar PFT completion (April 2027) and ICD timeline; ramp-up assumptions described as conservative and under review.
Q4 EBITDA margin of 21.2% partly driven by lower other expenses that management said may reverse; quarterly EBITDA per TEU volatility from commodity mix and auctions.
Pending capital call of about INR80 crores on the rights issue and private placement, and whether bank debt stays near INR100 crores.
Chennai capacity expansion details not yet disclosed; Mundra expansion scope unclear.
JNPT Speedy upgrade completion (around Q3 FY27) needed to lift throughput; terminal congestion and transport fleet shortage at JNPT noted as current seasonal issue.
Group-company dependence for Farrukhnagar construction and for first/last-mile services.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the 2030 aspiration, but cautious and somewhat evasive on specifics: Chennai timing, quarterly margin drivers and Farrukhnagar volume ramp were deferred to future calls. Management repeatedly pointed to multi-quarter trends rather than the Q4 spike.
key_quotes: We recorded our highest ever annual volumes, backed it up with disciplined yield management and the operating leverage due to capacity expansion, enabled EBITDA increase 26% year-on-year
So we are on course to achieve the 1 million laden TEU number in FY28.
But the steady-state number is what Pritam had said. What we would like to be is in the range of INR2,200 to INR2,400.
As of now, company doesn't have any debt on its balance sheet, and the company is debt free.

adds.what: Farrukhnagar PFT-ICD rail-linked facility, about 1.2 lakh TEU added in phases
JNPT Speedy Multimodes yard and warehouse upgrade (facility size unchanged, lifts throughput)
Chennai and Mundra expansions under 3-year plan (details not yet shared)

growth.why: Management reiterates 1 million laden TEU by FY28 and 12.5-13 lakh capacity by 2030, backed by Farrukhnagar PFT-ICD (~1.2 lakh TEU, PFT April 2027, ~INR200-226 cr capex) and JNPT upgrade (~INR20 cr, Q3 FY27), but the brief gives no volume growth number for FY27 and Chennai/Mundra details are pending.
